material_systems.name: Acrylic DTM Primer for Factory-Primed Steel Doors

products: Sherwin-Williams Pro Industrial DTM Acrylic Primer/Finish
Benjamin Moore Insl-X Stix DTM Bonding Primer
primer.notes: For factory-primed or pre-primed steel doors in sound or failing paint condition. Provides compatibility with existing factory primer. Apply to spot-prime bare areas or full-prime when >30% bare. Factory prime is transit protection only — does not count as field prime. Non-porous steel surface yields higher coverage than wood primers.

applies_when.condition: Standard primer for factory-primed steel doors. Use SYS_EXT_DRRP_PRIMER_ZINC for bare/rusted carbon steel or SYS_EXT_DRRP_PRIMER_ETCH for galvanized.

material_systems.notes: Default steel door primer for repaint. Most residential steel doors are factory-primed. DTM acrylic is compatible with factory primer systems and provides adhesion on smooth steel surfaces. If active rust is present, switch to SYS_EXT_DRRP_PRIMER_ZINC after SSPC debridement.

material_systems.name: Zinc-Rich Epoxy/Alkyd Primer for Bare or Rusted Carbon Steel

primer.type: Zinc-rich epoxy or alkyd rust-inhibiting primer
products: Benjamin Moore Insl-X Prime Lock Plus Alkyd Primer
Rustoleum Professional High Performance Enamel Primer
primer.notes: REQUIRED for bare carbon steel or steel with active rust after SSPC-SP3/SP6 debridement. Provides sacrificial barrier protection — zinc corrodes preferentially, protecting the steel substrate. Must be applied same day as bare metal exposure to prevent flash rusting. Lower coverage than DTM acrylic due to porous debrided surface and thicker film build requirement.

applies_when.condition: Active rust removed to bare metal via SSPC-SP3/SP6. Apply zinc-rich primer same day as metal exposure.

material_systems.notes: CRITICAL: Painting over rust without debridement causes underfilm corrosion. Zinc-rich primer provides cathodic (sacrificial) protection at the bare metal interface. This system is substrate-state-driven — triggered by SS_EXT_SURFACE_RUST, not by quality tier.

material_systems.name: Acrylic Etching Primer for Galvanized Steel Doors

primer.type: Acrylic etching primer / vinyl wash primer
products: Benjamin Moore Fresh Start High-Hiding Primer (for galvanized)
primer.notes: REQUIRED for galvanized or galvannealed steel doors. Chemically promotes adhesion on zinc-coated passive surfaces that repel standard primers. Standard acrylic primers will delaminate from galvanized steel within 6-12 months. Apply to spot-prime or full-prime as condition requires.

applies_when.condition: Galvanized steel surface identified during condition assessment

material_systems.notes: Galvanized steel is common on commercial and some residential steel doors. The zinc coating creates a passive surface that requires chemical bonding primer. If galvanized door also has active rust, debride rust areas and use SYS_EXT_DRRP_PRIMER_ZINC on debrided areas + SYS_EXT_DRRP_PRIMER_ETCH on intact galvanized areas.

material_systems.name: Standard Acrylic Exterior Primer for Wood Doors

products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec EXT Primer
PPG Sun Proof Exterior Latex Primer
primer.notes: Standard acrylic primer for wood doors with sound existing coating or standard softwood species (pine, fir, spruce). For tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood), use SYS_EXT_DRRP_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK instead. Also used as full-surface primer on fiberglass doors (100% acrylic compatible system). Door surface area ~21 SF per face (3'x7' standard).

applies_when.condition: Standard softwood species or fiberglass. Bare areas exposed during prep. For tannin-rich wood use SYS_EXT_DRRP_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK.

material_systems.notes: Dual-use: wood and fiberglass. 100% acrylic formulation is safe for fiberglass (permeable, allows outgassing escape). On fiberglass, this is the ONLY primer chemistry permitted — oil-based primers are strictly PROHIBITED. On wood doors, coverage is slightly lower than steel due to grain absorption.

material_systems.name: Alkyd Stain-Blocking Primer for Tannin-Rich Wood Doors

products: Benjamin Moore Fresh Start Alkyd Primer
primer.notes: REQUIRED for tannin-rich wood species (cedar, redwood, mahogany) when bare wood is exposed during scraping. Blocks water-soluble extractives that bleed through latex coatings as brown/yellow stains. Alkyd formulation is non-negotiable — latex primer on bare tannin-rich wood WILL bleed. Lower coverage due to absorptive open grain.

applies_when.condition: Bare tannin-rich wood (cedar, redwood, mahogany) exposed during scraping

material_systems.compatibility_warning: PROHIBITED on fiberglass doors. Alkyd/oil products cause outgassing blisters on fiberglass. Use SYS_EXT_DRRP_PRIMER_ACRYLIC for fiberglass.
material_systems.notes: Tannin-rich wood species override. When cedar or redwood bare wood is exposed during scraping, this system REPLACES the standard acrylic primer. Higher material consumption due to absorptive open grain on tannin-rich species.

material_systems.name: 100% Acrylic Exterior Enamel Finish for All Door Substrates

finish.type: 100% Acrylic Exterior Latex Enamel / Acrylic-Urethane Blend
finish.notes: Primary finish for ALL door substrates (steel, fiberglass, wood). 100% acrylic formulation is MANDATORY for fiberglass compatibility (permeability for outgassing escape). Safe and effective on steel and wood as well. Coverage per door: ~21 SF face area x 2 faces = ~42 SF per standard door. Complex geometry (panels, recesses, edges) reduces effective coverage 20-30% vs flat wall. 2 coats required at all tiers.

sheen_constraints.steel_max_gloss: ANSI A250.8 limits steel door gloss to 20% reflectance at 60 degrees. Satin or lower recommended for steel — high gloss emphasizes factory welding marks and surface imperfections.
sheen_constraints.fiberglass: Satin or low-lustre recommended per doctrine. Semi-gloss at QT4 acceptable on smooth/paint-grade fiberglass.
sheen_constraints.wood: Satin standard. Semi-gloss at QT4 accentuates grain detail — requires thorough prep.

material_systems.notes: Universal finish system across all three substrate materials. 100% acrylic chemistry is the common denominator that works for steel (durable), fiberglass (permeable), and wood (flexible). QT4 uses premium acrylic or acrylic-urethane blend for enhanced durability and flow.

material_systems.name: IR-Reflective Finish for Dark Colors (LRV <30)

finish.notes: MANDATORY when selected color LRV < 30 on sun-exposed doors. IR-reflective pigment technology drops surface temperature 20-30 degrees F, preventing thermal damage: wood joint failure, steel warping, fiberglass outgassing. This is a material SWAP — replaces SYS_EXT_DRRP_FINISH_ACRYLIC at higher cost, not an additional product. Slightly lower coverage than standard finish due to IR-reflective pigment loading (~8% reduction).

applies_when.condition: GATE CONDITION: dark color (LRV <30) on sun-exposed exterior door

material_systems.notes: Non-negotiable for dark colors on exterior doors regardless of substrate material. All three substrates (steel, fiberglass, wood) suffer from excessive heat absorption with dark colors. Without IR-reflective technology, surface temps can exceed 160 degrees F on south/west-facing doors.

spot_prime_area.notes: Spot prime on steel doors — affected bare area only. Non-porous surface yields highest primer coverage. Standard door face ~21 SF. Typical bare percentage: 5-10% on SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT, 15-30% on SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT.

assumptions: Coverage applies to affected area only — not full door face.
Steel is non-porous — consistent coverage regardless of state severity.
Bare percentage determined during condition assessment.

SS_EXT_SURFACE_RUST.notes: Full prime on debrided bare steel after SSPC-SP3/SP6. Surface is pitted and roughened from debridement — lower coverage than smooth factory steel. Thicker film build required for cathodic protection. Standard door = ~42 SF both faces.

assumptions: Full-surface prime after rust debridement — all bare metal areas require coverage.
Pitted/roughened surface from debridement absorbs more primer than smooth steel.
Must be applied same day as debridement to prevent flash rusting.

spot_prime_area_acrylic.notes: Spot prime on wood/fiberglass doors — affected bare area only. Standard softwoods and fiberglass use acrylic primer.

spot_prime_area_stainblock.notes: Spot prime on tannin-rich wood doors (cedar, redwood). Alkyd stain-block has lower coverage due to absorptive open grain.

assumptions: Coverage applies to affected area only — not full door face.
Bare percentage determined during condition assessment.
Tannin-rich species require alkyd stain-block even for spot priming.

SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT.notes: Full prime on failing wood doors (>30% bare). Mixed surface — some bare wood, some existing coating. Tannin-rich species consume 15-20% more primer. Standard door ~42 SF both faces + edges.

assumptions: Full-surface prime required when bare percentage >= 30%.
Standard door: ~21 SF per face x 2 faces + ~8 SF edges = ~50 SF total for six-side sealing.
Tannin-rich species: alkyd stain-block on all bare areas, acrylic on intact coating areas.

slab.notes: Flat face slab door. Minimal detail — best coverage. ~42 SF both faces + ~8 SF edges = ~50 SF total.

panel.notes: 6-panel or multi-panel door. Recesses, raised profiles, and multiple edges reduce effective coverage 10-15% vs slab. Same face area but more material consumed in panel detail.

grand_entry.notes: Grand entry with sidelites and transom. Complex geometry — multiple glass lites require cutting in, sidelite narrow rails consume more material per SF. Total surface area significantly larger (2-3x single door).

assumptions: Coverage is per EA door unit (all faces + edges).
2-coat system standard at QT3/QT4. QT5 may require 3 coats with interstage sanding.
IR-reflective finish: ~8% lower coverage than standard acrylic due to pigment loading.
Waste factor +15% — doors are detail brush/roller work with higher waste than field surfaces.
Grand entry SF includes sidelite panels and transom components.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush 2-2.5 inch
consumables.notes: Primary applicator for exterior door painting. 2 inch for panel detail and glass lite edges, 2.5 inch for flat slab faces and rail/stile surfaces. Angled sash for clean lines at glass edge, hardware pocket, and door-to-frame junction. Quality nylon/polyester blend for acrylic exterior coatings.

consumables.name: Detail brush 1-1.5 inch
consumables.notes: For tight areas: hinge mortises, strike plate pockets, panel moulding edges, weatherstrip channels. Critical for six-side sealing access on wood doors. Smaller brush reaches areas main sash brush cannot.

consumables.name: Mini foam/microfiber roller 4-6 inch
consumables.notes: For panel flats on steel and fiberglass doors. Foam roller produces smooth finish on non-porous surfaces without brush marks. Microfiber for wood grain. Not used on panel moulding edges (brush only). Speeds production on slab doors significantly.

consumables.name: Airless spray tips 311-413
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: application_method = spray. 311 for narrow rail/stile profiles, 413 for panel flats and slab faces. Fine fan pattern for door detail. Door spray produces superior finish quality on panel doors — no brush marks in panel recesses.

consumables.name: 60-mesh spray filter for latex
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: application_method = spray. Standard 60-mesh filter for latex exterior coatings. Change when flow rate drops.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 80 grit (heavy paint buildup / body filler rough)
consumables.notes: For steel dent body filler rough sanding and heavy paint buildup feathering. Also for QT5 full-strip prep work. CONDITIONAL: substrate_state = SS_EXT_SURFACE_RUST or quality_tier = QT5 restoration.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150 grit (feather-edge / adhesion)
consumables.notes: For feather-edge sanding at scraped areas and adhesion tooth on sound existing paint. Standard prep-stage abrasive for all substrate states on steel and wood. NOT for textured fiberglass — do not sand textured fiberglass doors.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220 grit (interstage / pre-finish)
consumables.notes: For interstage sanding between coats at QT4/QT5. Produces adhesion tooth without scratches visible in semi-gloss/gloss finish. Also for light scuff on smooth fiberglass (paint-grade only).

consumables.name: Sandpaper 300 grit (steel rust feathering / QT5 final)
consumables.notes: For feathering rust spot edges on steel until transition is imperceptible (per doctrine). Also for QT5 final interstage sand before topcoat. Fine grit minimizes scratch pattern visible in semi-gloss/gloss finish.

consumables.name: 2-component auto-body filler + hardener
consumables.notes: For steel door dent repair. 2-component polyester body filler from auto-body supply. Apply after 80-grit sanding, finish-sand with 240/300-grit. Also used at QT5 for surface perfection on all substrates (filling minor imperfections). Not a paint product — auto-body supply item.

consumables.name: Carbide scrapers (rigid and flexible)
consumables.notes: For removing loose and peeling paint. Carbide stays sharp longer than steel. Rigid for flat faces, flexible for panel profiles. CONDITIONAL: substrate_state = SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT. NOT for fiberglass — scraping fiberglass risks surface damage.

consumables.name: TSP cleaner / degreaser
consumables.notes: Trisodium phosphate or TSP substitute for surface cleaning on steel and wood doors. Mix per manufacturer directions. Used for general degreasing and contaminant removal before painting.

consumables.name: Denatured alcohol for fiberglass cleaning
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: substrate_material = fiberglass. Safe cleaning solvent for fiberglass doors. Removes contaminants without damaging resin matrix. Hydrocarbon solvents (xylene, acetone, MEK) are STRICTLY PROHIBITED on fiberglass — causes irreversible resin damage.

consumables.name: Tack cloth for dust removal
consumables.notes: Remove sanding dust before prime or finish coat. Critical at QT4/QT5 where dust nibs are visible in semi-gloss/gloss finish. Used after every sanding step.

consumables.name: Exterior polyurethane or hybrid polymer caulk (paintable)
consumables.notes: For door-to-frame junction caulk replacement. Polyurethane or MS hybrid polymer — paintable, exterior-grade, flexible. Replace all failed existing caulk during repaint. Standard door frame perimeter ~22 LF. NEVER use silicone — silicone prevents paint adhesion.

consumables.name: Caulk gun (dripless ratchet type)
consumables.notes: Dripless ratchet-type caulk gun for clean bead application. Standard tool — reusable.

consumables.name: Masking tape (exterior grade UV-resistant)
consumables.notes: UV-resistant exterior masking tape. 14-day removal rating minimum for multi-day exterior projects. Used for glass lite edge masking, threshold protection, weatherstrip deep-tape method, and siding adjacent protection.

consumables.name: Masking paper / kraft paper 12-18 inch
consumables.notes: For masking glass lites in panel doors and grand entry assemblies (sidelites, transom). Also for threshold/sill protection. Combined with masking tape for full glass coverage.

consumables.name: Masking film with tape edge (pre-taped poly)
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: application_method = spray or grand entry glass masking. Pre-taped plastic film for full glass and siding masking during spray application. Faster than paper/tape combo for large masking areas.

consumables.name: Narrow masking tape for weatherstrip deep-tape method
consumables.notes: Narrow (3/4 inch) masking tape pushed deep into the gap between jamb and weatherstripping with a putty knife. CONDITIONAL: weatherstrip cannot be removed (friction-fit removal preferred). Protects weatherstrip from paint contact — painted weatherstrip loses elasticity and seal function.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloth
consumables.notes: Ground protection under door work area. Catches drips, scraping debris, and sanding dust. When door is removed for spray or six-side access, drop cloth goes under sawhorses.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting 4 mil
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: application_method = spray. For landscape and hardscape protection from overspray during spray application. Also for siding/wall adjacent protection when spraying door on frame.

consumables.name: Zip-lock bags and labels for hardware storage
consumables.notes: Bag all removed hardware per door with label identifying door location. Prevents hardware mix-up across multi-door projects. Includes: lockset, deadbolt, strike plates, hinges (3-4), address numbers, knocker, peephole. Critical for proper reinstallation.

consumables.name: Lead test kits (EPA-recognized)
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: pre_1978 = true. EPA-recognized test kits (e.g., 3M LeadCheck). Required before disturbing paint on pre-1978 structures. Test at 3+ locations per door: face, edge, frame.

consumables.name: Polyethylene sheeting 6 mil (RRP containment)
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: pre_1978 = true AND lead_positive = true. 6-mil poly for ground containment extending 10 ft from door per EPA RRP rule. Heavier gauge than standard protection — must contain lead paint debris.

consumables.name: HEPA vacuum bags
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: pre_1978 = true AND lead_positive = true. For HEPA vacuum during and after lead-safe scraping. Required throughout prep phase when lead is present.

consumables.name: Lead-safe waste disposal bags
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: pre_1978 = true AND lead_positive = true. 6-mil bags for lead paint waste. Labeled per EPA requirements.

consumables.name: P100 respirator cartridges
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: pre_1978 = true AND lead_positive = true. P100 particulate filter for half-face respirator during lead paint disturbance.

consumables.name: Disposable coveralls (Tyvek)
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: pre_1978 = true AND lead_positive = true. Disposable coveralls prevent lead dust transfer. Required for all crew during lead paint disturbance.

ext_hardware_removal.description: Hardware removal and bagging — not masking. All hardware removed before prep begins.
ext_hardware_removal.notes: Hardware REMOVAL is the standard — masking is discouraged. Areas beneath masked hardware remain unsealed, creating moisture infiltration points. Remove all: lockset, deadbolt, strike plates, hinges, address numbers, knocker, peephole. Bag and label per door.

ext_glass_mask.description: Glass lite masking for panel doors and grand entry assemblies
ext_glass_mask.notes: Mask each individual glass lite. Grand entry sidelites and transoms add significant masking scope — may have 4-8 individual lites. Brush: tape at glass edge only. Spray: full glass cover with paper/film.

ext_weatherstrip_protect.description: Weatherstrip protection — pull out or deep-tape. NEVER paint.
ext_weatherstrip_protect.notes: Friction-fit stripping: pull out before painting, re-insert after dry. If removal impossible: push narrow tape deep into gap with putty knife. Painting weatherstripping destroys elasticity — NEVER paint. Fixed time per door, no PaintScope key needed (EA-based task).

ext_threshold_protect.description: Door threshold/sill plate protection from drips and overspray
ext_threshold_protect.notes: Tape and paper to prevent drips/overspray on threshold. Fixed per door. Threshold is not in painting scope — protection only.

ext_ground_cover.description: Ground surface protection under door work zone
ext_ground_cover.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray or when door is removed and set on sawhorses
ext_ground_cover.notes: Canvas drops at base of door work area. If spraying: full tarp under sawhorses. Scraping generates paint chips requiring containment — active during prep AND coating phases.

ext_siding_adjacent.description: Siding adjacent to door opening — mask during spray application
ext_siding_adjacent.notes: Masking paper/film on siding within overspray range when spraying door on frame. Not needed for brush application. Not needed when door is removed and sprayed away from opening.

compatibility_rules.description: Factory-primed steel, sound paint — spot DTM prime bare areas
compatibility_rules.notes: Existing factory primer is sound. Spot-prime bare areas only. No full prime needed if adhesion test passes.

compatibility_rules.description: Factory-primed steel, failing paint <30% bare — spot DTM prime
compatibility_rules.notes: Minor failure on factory-primed steel. Spot-prime scraped areas with DTM acrylic.

compatibility_rules.description: Factory-primed steel, failing paint >=30% bare — full DTM prime
compatibility_rules.notes: Extensive failure on factory-primed steel requires full prime.

compatibility_rules.description: Galvanized steel, sound paint — spot etch prime bare areas
compatibility_rules.notes: Galvanized surface requires etching primer even for spot priming. Standard DTM will not adhere.

compatibility_rules.description: Galvanized steel, failing paint — etch prime per bare percentage
compatibility_rules.notes: Spot prime if <30% bare. Full prime if >=30% bare. Etching primer required on all exposed galvanized areas.

compatibility_rules.description: Steel with active rust — SSPC debridement + zinc-rich prime (MANDATORY)
compatibility_rules.notes: CRITICAL: Active rust must be removed to bare metal. Painting over rust causes underfilm corrosion. Zinc-rich primer provides sacrificial barrier protection. Apply same day as debridement.

compatibility_rules.description: Fiberglass — 100% acrylic primer ONLY. Oil/alkyd PROHIBITED.
compatibility_rules.notes: HARD BLOCKER: Oil-based and alkyd products cause outgassing blisters on fiberglass under sun heat. Only 100% acrylic latex systems permitted. This is non-negotiable per every fiberglass door manufacturer.

compatibility_rules.description: Fiberglass — do NOT sand textured (stain-grade) doors
compatibility_rules.notes: Sanding destroys embossed wood-grain profile — irreversible damage requiring door replacement. Prep limited to cleaning only on textured fiberglass.

compatibility_rules.description: Wood, standard softwood — acrylic primer on bare areas
compatibility_rules.notes: Standard softwoods (pine, fir, spruce): acrylic primer on bare areas. Spot if <30% bare. Full if >=30% bare.

compatibility_rules.description: Wood, tannin-rich species — alkyd stain-block on bare areas
compatibility_rules.notes: Tannin-rich override. Cedar/redwood bare exposure requires alkyd stain-blocker — latex primer on bare tannin-rich wood WILL bleed.

compatibility_rules.description: LRV <30 on sun-exposed door — IR-reflective finish MANDATORY
compatibility_rules.notes: GATE CONDITION. Dark colors (LRV <30) on exterior doors absorb excessive heat. IR-reflective coating drops surface temp 20-30 degrees F. Prevents wood joint failure, steel warping, and fiberglass outgassing. Non-negotiable.
Standard finish for all substrates when color LRV is >=30. No IR-reflective technology needed.

compatibility_rules.description: Steel doors — max gloss = satin per ANSI A250.8
compatibility_rules.notes: ANSI A250.8 (SDI 100): maximum paint gloss = 20% reflectance at 60-degree gloss meter. Semi-gloss and gloss emphasize factory welding marks and surface imperfections. Satin or lower recommended.

QT5 (fine finish / restoration) requires 2-coat primer system with interstage sanding between all coats. 4 total coating passes minimum. Body filler for all imperfections. Mirror-smooth finish standard.

All six sides of wood door must be sealed. Door removal from frame required to access all edges. Bottom edge end-grain is primary moisture wicking failure point. Manufacturer warranty requires all six sides sealed within 2-30 days.

compatibility_rules.description: Fiberglass cleaning — mild soap or denatured alcohol ONLY
compatibility_rules.notes: Hydrocarbon solvents damage fiberglass resin matrix. Creates pitting, softening, and loss of structural integrity. Damage is irreversible.

compatibility_rules.description: Pre-1978 with paint disturbance — RRP supplies required
compatibility_rules.notes: EPA RRP Rule (40 CFR 745) requires lead-safe work practices for pre-1978 homes when disturbing >2 SF on building exterior. Exterior doors historically received oil-based lead paint — HIGH RISK surface.

compatibility_rules.description: NEVER silicone caulk at door-to-frame junction
compatibility_rules.notes: Silicone prevents paint adhesion and is not paintable. Use polyurethane or MS hybrid polymer caulk at door-to-frame junction. Must be paintable and exterior-rated.

risk_notes.topic: Outgassing blisters on fiberglass from oil-based products
risk_notes.risk: Oil-based primers or topcoats on fiberglass doors trap manufacturing outgassing vapors under sun heat, causing blistering from within the door substrate. Blisters appear months to years after application.
risk_notes.mitigation: HARD BLOCKER: Use ONLY 100% acrylic latex systems on fiberglass. Oil-based products strictly prohibited. Verify substrate material during condition assessment BEFORE selecting products.

risk_notes.topic: Underfilm corrosion from painting over rust on steel
risk_notes.risk: Rust painted over without proper debridement continues electrolytic action beneath the paint film. Moisture travels via capillary action under primer. Corrosion expands outward, lifting paint in expanding circles.
risk_notes.mitigation: Remove ALL active rust to bare metal via SSPC-SP3/SP6. Feather edges with 300-grit. Apply zinc-rich primer same day. Do NOT spot-prime over rust — debridement is mandatory.

risk_notes.topic: Thermal warping from dark color without IR-reflective coating
risk_notes.risk: Low-LRV dark colors absorb excessive solar heat. Surface temperatures can exceed 160 degrees F on south/west-facing doors. Causes joint separation (wood), thermal distortion (steel), and outgassing (fiberglass).
risk_notes.mitigation: Mandatory IR-reflective coating for LRV <30. Verify sun exposure and color selection during scope capture. Document color LRV approval before ordering.

risk_notes.topic: Moisture wicking through unsealed wood end-grain
risk_notes.risk: Wood door rails (top/bottom) and edges act as capillary networks. Unsealed end-grain absorbs water rapidly, causing swelling, joint failure, and coating delamination from inside out.
risk_notes.mitigation: Six-side sealing mandatory. Door must be removed from frame. Bottom edge requires extra attention. Verify all six sides sealed within manufacturer timeframe.

risk_notes.risk: Hydrocarbon solvents (xylene, acetone, MEK, lacquer thinner) on fiberglass damage the polymer resin matrix. Creates pitting, softening, and irreversible loss of structural integrity.
risk_notes.mitigation: Clean fiberglass with mild dish soap or denatured alcohol ONLY. Training protocol must distinguish steel cleaning (solvent OK) from fiberglass cleaning (solvent prohibited).

risk_notes.risk: Sanding textured (stain-grade) fiberglass destroys embossed wood-grain profile. Irreversible damage requiring door replacement. Cannot be restored.
risk_notes.mitigation: Do NOT sand textured fiberglass doors. Verify door grade (stain-grade vs paint-grade) before prep begins. Smooth/paint-grade may accept light scuff sanding only.

risk_notes.risk: Cedar and redwood contain water-soluble extractives that bleed through latex coatings as brown/yellow stains when bare wood is exposed.
risk_notes.mitigation: Alkyd stain-blocking primer mandatory on tannin-rich species when bare wood is exposed. Latex primer on bare cedar/redwood WILL bleed.

risk_notes.topic: Lead paint on pre-1978 exterior doors
risk_notes.risk: Exterior doors historically received oil-based lead paint. HIGH RISK surface for lead. Scraping without RRP containment disperses lead dust — EPA violation and health hazard.
risk_notes.mitigation: Test all pre-1978 doors before any paint disturbance. Full RRP containment, wet scraping, HEPA vacuum, lead-safe disposal when lead is present.

risk_notes.risk: When multiple doors have hardware removed simultaneously, hardware can be mixed up during reinstall. Wrong hardware = misaligned strikes, non-functional locks, cosmetic mismatch.
risk_notes.mitigation: Bag and label all hardware per door with door location identifier. Do not commingle hardware from different doors.

material_quantity_notes.ea_based_estimation: Doors are estimated per EA, not SF. All material quantities are derived from standard door face area (~21 SF per face, ~42 SF both faces, ~50 SF including edges for six-side seal). Grand entry multiply by component count.
material_quantity_notes.waste_factor: +15% for door painting — detail brush/roller work with higher waste than field surfaces.
material_quantity_notes.spray_transfer_efficiency: When application_method = spray: multiply material quantity by 1.20-1.25 for 60-70% transfer efficiency. Door spray has better transfer than siding (closer distance, contained target) but still has overspray losses.
material_quantity_notes.two_coat_standard: 2 finish coats at all quality tiers (QT3/QT4/QT5). No single-coat option — doors are fine-finish substrate. QT5 adds 2-coat primer (4 total coating passes).
material_quantity_notes.complexity_material_impact: Panel doors consume 10-15% more finish material than slab due to recesses and profiles. Grand entry consumes 2-3x standard door material due to sidelites, transom, and increased total surface area.
material_quantity_notes.ir_reflective_material_premium: IR-reflective finish costs approximately 15-25% more per gallon than standard acrylic and has ~8% lower coverage. Material cost impact is significant for dark-color door projects.
material_quantity_notes.six_side_primer_wood: Wood doors receiving six-side seal require primer on all edges including bottom end-grain. Additional ~8 SF per door (perimeter edges) beyond face area.

assumptions.value: ~21 SF per face (3'x7' standard door). ~42 SF both faces. ~50 SF total with edges for six-side seal.
assumptions.note: Standard residential entry door. Grand entry sidelite panels add ~10-15 SF each. Transom adds ~5-10 SF.

assumptions.value: Door coverage 300-400 SF/gal vs wall 350-450 SF/gal — 20-30% lower effective coverage due to complex geometry
assumptions.note: Panel recesses, raised profiles, and edges reduce effective coverage compared to flat wall surfaces.

assumptions.value: ~8% lower coverage than standard acrylic finish due to IR-reflective pigment loading
assumptions.source: Product data sheets for VinylSafe/IR-reflective product lines
assumptions.note: No direct doctrine coverage for IR-reflective product coverage rates on doors. Derived from manufacturer PDS data and sibling trim spec pattern. Flag for field calibration.

assumptions.value: 300-400 SF/gal — lower coverage on pitted/roughened surface from SSPC debridement
assumptions.source: Product data sheets; industry practice for debrided metal surfaces
assumptions.note: Doctrine specifies zinc-rich primer for bare steel but does not provide coverage rates specific to debrided surface profiles. Derived from manufacturer data.

assumptions.value: 1 TUBE per 3-4 doors — standard door frame perimeter ~22 LF, typical joint width 1/4 inch
assumptions.source: Calculated from standard door frame dimensions; sibling spec caulk rate (1 TUBE per 30 LF)
assumptions.note: Assumes ~7 LF caulk per door (not full perimeter — only failing/open joints). Varies by condition.

assumptions.value: QT5 uses QT4-tier finish products (premium acrylic) but with 2-coat primer, interstage sanding, and higher process standard
assumptions.note: QT5 difference is process (more coats, interstage sand, body filler, mirror-smooth standard) not product chemistry. Emerald-tier products permitted but not required.

uncertainty_flags.detail: Grand entry door assemblies (sidelites + transom) vary significantly in size and configuration. The 2-3x material multiplier vs standard door is approximate.
uncertainty_flags.recommendation: Capture actual component count and individual panel dimensions during scope assessment for accurate material estimation.

uncertainty_flags.detail: Distinguishing factory-primed vs galvanized vs carbon steel requires inspection skill. Wrong identification leads to wrong primer system (adhesion failure).
uncertainty_flags.recommendation: Include steel type identification checklist in condition assessment protocol. Magnet test for ferrous. Visual inspection for galvanized coating.

uncertainty_flags.detail: Stain-grade (textured) vs paint-grade (smooth) fiberglass must be correctly identified before prep to avoid sanding textured doors. Incorrect identification = irreversible damage.
uncertainty_flags.recommendation: Include fiberglass grade identification in condition assessment protocol. Document with photos.
